q-265756.name: Question 1
q-265756.problem:
Compute the gradient of the function $f:{R}^{4}\to R$ defined by 

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot x
$$

 with respect to $x$ at $x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
q-265756.worked_solution:
Writing $b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$, we have

$$
f(x)={b}^{T}x.
$$

The gradient of a function $f(x)={b}^{T}x$ with respect to $x\in {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{∇}_{x}f(x)=b.
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
{∇}_{x}f(x)=b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

a
12sign(w)+w
b
12(‖w‖1)2⋅sign(w)+x
c
12sign(w)+2x
d
6sign(w)+x
e
12(‖w‖1)2⋅sign(w)+w
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Using the results ∇w(‖w‖1)=sign(w),∇w(xTw)=x, we have

∇wf=∇w(4(‖w‖1)3+xTw)=∇w(4(‖w‖1)3)+∇w(xTw)=4⋅∇w((‖w‖1)3)+∇w(xTw)=4⋅3(‖w‖1)2⋅∇w(‖w‖1)+x=4⋅3(‖w‖1)2⋅sign(w)+x=12(‖w‖1)2⋅sign(w)+x.
